The repository owns this board. [Workflow and record format](tasks/README.md).

**Status is not authorization.** A task, dependency, or green check never grants permission
to commit, push, merge, deploy, send, delete, or access production data. **Ready** is the
owner's queue: any agent may execute a Ready task. Publishing follows AGENTS.md ›
"Delegation And Merge Policy". An open draft PR moving a task to In progress is its claim.

Evidence marked **recorded** is a carried-forward claim, not fresh verification.
A checked PR proves its GitHub state, not product acceptance or production behavior.

The guard refuses a range from the newest deploy/* tag that mixes a deploy-alone change with any other shipped change, and prints the steps. It also refuses when there is no deploy tag yet; --allow-batch, on the owner's word, lets either through. Once the live version is read, it refuses when production's Worker is not the newest tag's (a rollback, a secret change or a dashboard edit), showing the live deployment's source; only --accept-live with the single live version id, on the owner's word, clears that, and the tag message records it. After the propagation loop, status smoke and security headers pass, the script tags the deployed commit deploy/&lt;UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHHMMZ&gt;-&lt;sha7&gt;. The message carries the commit, the UTC time, the Worker version (from WRANGLER_OUTPUT_FILE_PATH), the rollback version (from the pre-deploy wrangler deployments status), the SPA entry, the previous tag and any allowed batch. It pushes only that ref (git push --no-follow-tags), and exits 3 with the push command if the tag cannot be created or pushed (the deploy stands). If the script stops after the upload (a failed check, SIGTERM or SIGHUP), the EXIT trap prints how to tag the deploy should the owner keep it; a failed wrangler deploy says to check deployments status. pnpm release:status reports the newest tag, the merges since with shipped and owner-gate classes, and "deploy due" with steps or "nothing to ship". Shipped means apps/api, apps/web, packages and seven root build inputs (.nvmrc and .npmrc included), minus tests and fixtures, Markdown outside apps/web/public/, and repo tools. The newest tag is the latest created. Deploy-alone means a shipped file matched by owner-gate GATES, imported unchanged. The runbook, start-session steps 5 and 9, close-session §5 and AGENTS.md describe it. Post-merge acceptance (backfilling the 1eed288 tag, the first real tagged deploy) is RF-245. The owner-gate coverage gap for scripts/release-status.mjs is RF-246. | checked 2026-11-24 |

| [RF-195](tasks/RF-195.json) RF-129 routing follow-ups from the #725 final review | P3 / task | needs RF-129 | All seven items met on #728 (Neo, 2026-11-06). (1) A refreshed /classes/&lt;id&gt;/live reuses the run payload the class detail read fetched: loadDetail returns it and restoreClass uses it, fetching again only when that read failed. (2) Back/Forward from another destination to the class still selected and loaded shows the class again, re-owning the detail workspace, with no getClass, track or payload read. (3) /sign-in?error=&lt;code&gt; shows one plain-words Apple sign-in error on the form (“Apple sign-in didn’t finish. Try again, or use your email.”, whatever the code), then drops the code from the URL once the session check has settled. One message, not a cancelled/failed split, kept the entry bundle under its 180 kB budget (179.98 kB). (4) Dashboard tests wait for a queued stepTo Back with settleAppRouteForTests, which resolves on that popstate, not on a setTimeout(0). (5) Decision (owner approved the default, 2026-11-06): keep stepTo’s return-goes-Back design. It is what keeps the browser Back and Forward a true record of the visit (an exit or close returns to the entry it came from instead of stacking a duplicate), its state is two flags in app-route.ts, and plain pushes would make Back after every close re-open the screen just left. (6) The legacy /?auth= redirect is redirectLegacyAuthIntent in app-route.ts, called once in main.tsx before the first render. (7) Signed in on any path but Sign in or Sign up clears the remembered return-to. | checked 2026-11-04; checked 2026-11-06; checked 2026-11-07 |

| [RF-201](tasks/RF-201.json) Live queue readiness retry: race guard, announcements and one state source (RF-163 review follow-ups) | P3 / task | — | All five items met on #746 (Neo, 2026-11-06). (1) Every run-payload read of a queue class, from the candidate effect or a Retry, takes that class’s next token; only its newest read may land, and only while the class is still in the queue. A Retry overtaken by a candidate change is dropped, and a class removed during its Retry leaves no orphan result to show when it is added back. (2) A hidden status line announces “Checking readiness for &lt;class&gt;…” when a Retry starts and its outcome when it lands (can run live / checked: not ready to run yet / still couldn’t check). (3) The retry flag is LivePayloadState’s error variant with refreshing: true; the separate retrying set is gone, and the effect and the Retry share one read helper (readLivePayload). (4) Owner default (2026-11-06): the queue holds its order until the instructor acts. A retried card ranks by the result it had before its Retry, so it keeps its place and the copper does not move; a candidate change or a new ordering ranks from the latest results. The ranking comment says so. (5) The busy Checking… button is dimmed (opacity-60) with a spinning mark (motion-safe), besides cursor-progress and aria-disabled. | checked 2026-11-05; checked 2026-11-06; checked 2026-11-07 |
